name: GTx-027

lead: GTx-027 is an arylpropionamide-class SARM associated with GTx, Inc., investigated for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence and occasionally listed by muscle-building readers among SARMs.

SARMs are designed to activate androgen receptors selectively. A 2017 mouse study examined whether tissue-selective SARMs increase pelvic floor muscle mass in ovariectomized mice. Its status is listed as Phase I, discontinued, or preclinical, and no human trial on muscle or appearance exists.

paras: It is not marketed, and no routine for physique use exists.
No human safety data are available in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.

lead: GTx-027 is an investigational, orally taken non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the arylpropionamide class, developed by GTx, Inc. and a structural analogue of enobosarm (ostarine, GTx-024). SARMs are of interest to people who want muscle and strength gains, since androgen receptor activation in muscle and bone is how androgens build lean mass; in animals GTx-027 raised lean mass and muscle strength.[1][2][3]

GTx-027 was studied for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence and was never marketed. Sources differ on how far it progressed: some describe it as preclinical, others as reaching Phase I before being discontinued.[1][3] A 2017 mouse study examined whether the tissue-selective SARMs GTx-024 and GTx-027 restore pelvic floor muscle mass in ovariectomized mice, motivated by the lack of oral treatments for stress urinary incontinence.[2]
No physique or appearance trials exist. GTx-027 is not described as a common gray-market product; its sibling enobosarm is, and appears in anti-doping cases.[4][5]
infobox: Phase I, discontinued, or preclinical; sources differ[1][3]

paras: GTx-027 is a nonsteroidal androgen receptor modulator with mixed effects, acting as both an agonist and an antagonist depending on tissue. In laboratory studies it slowed the growth of androgen receptor-expressing breast cancer cells, and in animal studies it increased pelvic floor muscle weight in ovariectomized female rodents and raised body weight, lean mass and muscle strength.[3]

The pelvic floor is rich in androgen receptors, and researchers proposed SARMs as possible oral therapy for stress urinary incontinence; a 2017 study in ovariectomized mice reported that GTx-024 and GTx-027 restored pelvic muscles to the weight seen in sham-operated animals, with a trend toward higher total lean mass that was not statistically significant.[2] The related SARM enobosarm did not meet its endpoint in a Phase II trial for stress urinary incontinence and was abandoned.[1][5]

For context, enobosarm in two phase 3 trials in cancer-related muscle wasting increased lean body mass by roughly 0.4 to 0.5 kg without improving stair-climb power, and in a phase 2 study in healthy elderly people increased lean mass by about 1.3 kg over placebo.[5]

SARMs are not FDA approved but are sold online, and athletes' use has led to positive tests across several sports bodies, according to a 2023 systematic review poster.[4] WADA has banned the class since 2008.[1][5] GTx-027 itself is not described as a common gray-market product.
No studies found for GTx-027 in humans for appearance or muscle gain. The available research on its therapeutic areas is preclinical, such as the mouse pelvic-floor study.[2][3]
